subject.title: fix(acp): preserve structured exec approval metadata

question: When an exec approval event supplies a toolCallId that matches no pending tool call, should ACP reject that event or ignore the identifier and route it to the sole prompt for the session?
rationale: This choice trades legacy tolerance against authorization correlation integrity; repository policy treats approval fallbacks as explicit product and security decisions rather than implementation conveniences.

options.title: Reject explicit mismatches
options.body: Use session-only fallback only when toolCallId is absent, preventing contradictory identifiers from routing an approval to an unrelated prompt.

options.title: Preserve compatibility fallback
options.body: Keep routing an unmatched identifier to a sole session prompt, with explicit owner acceptance and real proof that stale or incomplete tool-call tracking requires this behavior.

recommendation.title: Reject explicit mismatches
recommendation.body: Use session-only fallback only when toolCallId is absent, preventing contradictory identifiers from routing an approval to an unrelated prompt.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the ACP approval relay and are the strongest history-backed owner for its correlation and compatibility semantics.
